      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya</link>
      <description><p>Ukraine’s security service says seven drones were launched from mothership in operation that sank Merkury warship</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/23/russia-ukraine-war-zelenskyy-libya-benghazi-drone-attack-ship-merkury-un-nato-europe-latest-news-updates">Europe live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya</a> on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.</p><p>Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.       <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <title>Bank of England directors illegally profited from post-abolition enslavement in Cuba</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba</link>
      <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Estonia has continued to deny it has allowed Ukrainian drones to operate from its territory despite repeated unsubstantiated claims from the Kremlin</p><p><strong>Turning to Ukraine, Nato’s Rutte stresses the need to secure the flow of “crucial supplies” or air defence weapons and ammunition to Ukraine.</strong></p><p><em><strong>“</strong>It helps Ukraine to defend itself today, but it also strengthens Ukraine’s hands in any future negotiations with Russia. … But support needs to be concrete. <strong>We have to show Putin that his attempts to weaken our support will fail.”</strong></em></p><p><em>“Our citizens need to know that the lights will stay on, that their homes will stay warm, that hospitals, transport and communications will keep working.”</em></p><p><em>“One day it can be in the form of an arson attack against a factory or drones disrupt disrupting an airport. The next, it is sabotaged railways or cargo vessels targeted at sea and cyber-attacks.”</em></p><p><em>“It’s all happening now, and it won’t go away anytime soon. … <strong>The conclusion of all of this is that we are all targeted,</strong> that we are all affected – when it comes to our pipelines, our cables, our energy grids and our economies – and they are all interconnected. … That means that we are all in this for the long term, and <strong>therefore we must step up to the plate, to ensure that, we stay ahead of danger.”</strong></em></p><p><em>“But if we are serious about keeping our alliance strong and secure, then <strong>all allies must pull their weight not only in 2035, but starting now.</strong> At least, everybody needs to have the credible path to get there.”</em></p><p><em>“These investments are also a boon to prosperity. There are dividends to be gained from investing more in defence. This is about real jobs for real people.”</em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/23/russia-ukraine-war-zelenskyy-libya-benghazi-drone-attack-ship-merkury-un-nato-europe-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Arctic air brings colder temperatures to Europe this week</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/23/arctic-air-colder-temperatures-europe-this-week</link>
      <description><p>After a warmer-than-average November so far globally, a cold snap is on the horizon in parts of Europe</p><p>While average global temperatures continue to set records through one of the strongest <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/elnino">El Niños</a> on record, temperatures across a large swathe of Europe could plunge this week, as Arctic air sweeps in.</p><p>On Friday, the global average temperature was 2.12C higher than the preindustrial average, the <a href="https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/earth-just-saw-the-most-anomalously-hot-day-ever-on-record/">biggest ever anomaly</a> and equivalent to 1.22C above the 1991-2020 climate average.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/23/arctic-air-colder-temperatures-europe-this-week">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/chamonix-mayor-tourist-limits-lac-blanc</link>
      <description><p>Rising numbers around Lac Blanc are having big impact on environment and on visitors’ enjoyment, mayor says</p><p>In the Alpine town of Chamonix, most tourist paths lead to the national park with spectacular views across Mont Blanc and the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2013/mar/31/alps-skiing-climate-change">shrinking blue glaciers</a>. In the summer, up to 4,000 tourists a day hike or take the cable car to the lakes high in the Aiguilles Rouges nature reserve.</p><p>Many of them descend disappointed. Once a place of nature and tranquility, the beauty spot’s visitor numbers have more than doubled since 2020, spoiling the experience and leaving trails of litter, threatening the environment and wildlife.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/chamonix-mayor-tourist-limits-lac-blanc">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>From mocked to mainstream: how Spain’s far-right Vox transformed its fortunes</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/vox-party-spain-far-right-mocked-to-mainstream</link>
      <description><p>Party that won just 0.2% of the vote in 2016 is on course for almost 20% this time and could be part of next government</p><p>Almost exactly eight years ago, a video clip of a stocky, bearded man riding a horse through western Andalucía <a href="https://www.antena3.com/noticias/espana/santiago-abascal-vox-caballo-reconquistar-andalucia-video_201811135beaadcc0cf200fa81f731e1.html">went viral in Spain</a>. The rider was Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party, the soundtrack was a bombastic snatch of the Lord of the Rings score, and the caption was an equally unsubtle callback to the 700-year fight to wrest the Iberian peninsula from Islamic rule. <em>“La Reconquista comenzará en tierras andaluzas,”</em> it read – the reconquest will begin on Andalucían soil.</p><p>Celebrated by some, jeered by others – and <a href="https://x.com/Proscojoncio/status/1061981999861325824">inventively lampooned</a> by those with sufficient skill and time on their hands – the video didn’t seem quite as amusing three weeks later when Vox <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/dec/09/far-right-andalucia-seville-vox-party-shockwave-spanish-politics">broke through into the political mainstream</a> by winning 12 seats in Andalucía’s regional parliament.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/vox-party-spain-far-right-mocked-to-mainstream">Continue reading...</a></description>

French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efe09190-dcbf-11f1-9487-5f60e87d1ec6</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 04:33:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg">© Abdul Saboor, POOL/AFP/File</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-top-contemporary-french-artist-christian-boltanski-dies-aged-76</link><description>
Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>
Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2534ffb8-8980-11ec-8ce4-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 12:31:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sharon GAFFNEY</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says world leaders have made 'stupid' comments on France riots based on fake AI videos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261021-macron-says-world-leaders-have-made-stupid-comments-on-france-riots-based-on-fake-ai-videos</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>
Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4e47fa4-88f4-11ec-97bf-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 10:43:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png">© FMM Graphic Studio</source><dc:creator>Tracy MCNICOLL</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teen wounds headmaster and teacher after opening fire at French school</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-french-police-arrest-14-year-old-after-two-teaching-staff-wounded-by-hunting-rifle-fire</link><description>
Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">de062bda-c61f-11f1-828c-2d5a86616301</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg">© Lou Benoist, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France 2022: The Choice</category><title>Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/france-2022-the-campaign/20220207-battle-for-the-far-right-zemmour-le-pen-fight-to-steal-each-other-s-thunder</link><description>
As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ecf0724-8861-11ec-862b-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Feb 2022 22:00:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PERELMAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261011-a-profile-of-rapha%C3%ABl-glucksmann-the-man-who-wants-to-be-french-president</link><description>
Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential elections, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <title>Nvidia shares surge 33% on Jensen Huang‘s return, adding $1tn to company’s value – business live</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/23/tech-sell-off-ai-stock-market-support-measures-deployed-south-korea-taiwan-china-ftse-nasdaq-latest-news-updates</link>
      <description><p>Donald Trump hails Huang as a ‘great patriot and national treasure’ after his surprise reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-chief-executive"><strong>Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO</strong></a></p></li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>Shares in UK housebuilder Crest Nicholson have slumped by a quarter, to a record low, after the company issued a profits warning this morning.</strong></p><p>Full year completions were 1,353, at the bottom end of the Group’s previous guidance range of 1,350 to 1,400 completions.</p><p>The warning has hammered Crest Nicholson shares, which have lost more than a quarter of their value this morning, currently trading down over 30%. The brutal sell-off is also weighing on the wider sector, dragging peers like Barratt Redrow, Persimmon, Vistry and Bellway into the red.</p><p>Today’s update suggests that weakness in the housing market is no longer confined to first-time buyers. Crest Nicholson is predominantly exposed to the mid-premium family housing market, and the sharp deterioration in sales rates indicates that more affluent upsizers are also becoming increasingly cautious amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/23/tech-sell-off-ai-stock-market-support-measures-deployed-south-korea-taiwan-china-ftse-nasdaq-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/23/thanksgiving-air-travel-us-explainer</link>
      <description><p>Amid air chaos, travelers will have to navigate an outdated system (and complex company policies if it all goes wrong)</p><p>Millions of people are planning to fly in the US over the Thanksgiving holiday, just two weeks after the US Federal Aviation Administration’s 13 November <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/faa-ground-stop-flights-explained">ground stop</a> halted all flights nationwide for the first time since 9/11.(Aside from a brief halt in 2023.)</p><p>In the chaos that ensued, some travelers embarked on <a href="https://www.reddit.com/r/royalcaribbean/comments/1xvkopq/comment/19smxjywidlcw/?context=3">overnight drives</a> to catch cruise ships and <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/women-stranded-faa-ground-stop-buy-ford-bronco-27-hour-road-trip-rcna609629">bought new cars</a> to make business meetings. Many had to simply cancel their plans and incur the costs that came with it. Over 18,000 flights were cancelled at a potential cost to travelers of $1.9bn in lost time and related expenses, <a href="https://www.andersoneconomicgroup.com/analysis-nationwide-ground-stop-cost-travelers-nearly-2-billion/">Anderson Economic Group estimates</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/23/thanksgiving-air-travel-us-explainer">Continue reading...</a></description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dee6caee-e728-11f1-80df-9f0d9c8f7db3</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:45:02 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg">© Carla Bernhardt/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261122-french-right-backs-macron-s-plan-to-put-public-spending-limits-in-constitution</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4bea9e76-e66c-11f1-b8f3-f96315fbf1b4</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:09:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg">AFP - STEPHANIE LECOCQ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-students-and-unions-unite-for-sixth-weekend-of-protests-across-france</link><description>
Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.

France is braced for its second nationwide strike in less than a fortnight on Tuesday, after unions called on nearly six million public-sector workers to take to the streets to demand higher wages.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/470371ba-e05b-11f1-9950-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T153531Z-25633910-RC2PNOAZ102X-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/470371ba-e05b-11f1-9950-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T153531Z-25633910-RC2PNOAZ102X-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">678bf058-e266-11f1-92d6-39b0dbf095fa</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:01:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/470371ba-e05b-11f1-9950-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T153531Z-25633910-RC2PNOAZ102X-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French actor Depardieu withdraws appeal against conviction for sexual assault</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261116-french-actor-depardieu-withdraws-appeal-against-conviction-for-sexual-assault</link><description>
French actor Gérard Depardieu has apologised after withdrawing his appeal against a May 2025 conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">514af00c-e1a1-11f1-82bc-0f0371ba9765</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:19:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French cybercrime unit probes massive cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261116-french-cybercrime-unit-probes-massive-cyberattack-on-la-poste-subsidiary</link><description>
A French anti-cybercrime unit was on Monday investigating a massive cyberattack which targeted a subsidiary of the La Poste group mid-September. The contact details of 22 million people were exposed during the attack, the Paris prosecutor's office confirmed on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f7093a68-e114-11f1-aa3b-e18acb043b04</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:01:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg">REUTERS - ERIC GAILLARD</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Harki families take legal action over children's 'ghost graves' in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-harki-families-take-legal-action-over-children-s-ghost-graves-in-france</link><description>

      <title>‘Celebrate, inspire, unite’: UK confirmed as host of 2035 Women’s World Cup</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/uk-confirmed-hosts-2035-womens-world-cup-fifa</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Country’s first World Cup since men’s 1966 edition in England</p></li><li><p>Bid lists 22 stadiums as potential venues</p></li></ul><p>The UK is to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup, Fifa has confirmed. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will stage the first World Cup hosted in the country since the 1966 men’s tournament in England.</p><p>The UK bid was the only one under consideration for 2035. The 2031 tournament has been awarded, also uncontested, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/2031-womens-world-cup-projection-fifa-ussf">to the United States, Mexico, ⁠Costa Rica and Jamaica</a>. The decisions were formalised at a virtual meeting of Fifa’s national associations on Monday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/uk-confirmed-hosts-2035-womens-world-cup-fifa">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Manchester United to appeal against Leny Yoro red card in defeat by Liverpool</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/manchester-united-appeal-leny-yoro-red-card-liverpool</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Mauricio Pochettino said after game it was ‘never a foul’</p></li><li><p>‘No one’s coming to save us,’ admits Kobbie Mainoo </p></li></ul><p>Manchester United intend to appeal against the red card Leny Yoro received in the eighth minute of the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">4-0 defeat at Liverpool</a> on Sunday. The defender was dismissed after fouling Alexander Isak outside the penalty area but Mauricio Pochettino believes the striker would not have reached the ball to take him through on goal against Senne Lammens and therefore it was <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/mauricio-pochettino-manchester-united-reign-begins-with-anfield-humiliation-liverpool">not worthy of a sending-off</a>.</p><p>United’s head coach said: “I don’t agree because the ball wasn’t in Isak’s control. Leny was running with him and when Isak saw the control wasn’t good and the ball was going to the keeper it is normal you delay, you stop running, and you wait to feel the touch and you go down. It is never a foul.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/manchester-united-appeal-leny-yoro-red-card-liverpool">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Emery insists no change of plan for Aston Villa despite fears over Galatasaray surface</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/unai-emery-no-change-of-plan-aston-villa-galatasaray-surface</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>‘Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible,’ says Villa manager</p></li><li><p>Turkish champions had to move game on Saturday</p></li></ul><p>Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions Leaguegame at Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”.</p><p>Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum time to recover after heavy maintenance work.       <description><p>German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds</p><p>It was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league.       <title>Teenage ace Williams-Barnett puts Tottenham on path to win over Ipswich</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/tottenham-ipswich-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich.</p><p>That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/tottenham-ipswich-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-premier-league">that the new manager</a> bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.</p><p>Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘Haaland must be worried’: Thierno Barry’s rise has David Moyes purring</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/thierno-barry-rise-david-moyes-purring-everton</link>
      <description><p>Everton striker has worked hard to find his scoring touch after admitting he hit ‘rock bottom’ at times last season</p><p>A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit.</p><p>“Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/06/everton-coventry-premier-league-match-report">a double against Coventry</a> took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/thierno-barry-rise-david-moyes-purring-everton">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action</link>
      <description><p>Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself</p><p>What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. <strong>Jamie Jackson</strong></p><p>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United</a></p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/mauricio-pochettino-manchester-united-reign-begins-with-anfield-humiliation-liverpool">‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision</a></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out</link>
      <description><p>Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement</p><p>César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like <em>not</em> being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.</p><p>It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘Obviously it’s not good’: Arteta sweating over David Raya’s fitness after injury</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/david-raya-shoulder-injury-arsenal-newcastle-mikel-arteta</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Keeper close to tears at Newcastle after hurting shoulder</p></li><li><p>Arsenal held 2-2, with Jaissle hailing ‘excellent’ display</p></li></ul><p>Arsenal were left sweating on the fitness of their goalkeeper David Raya after the Spaniard was forced off with a shoulder injury during the second half of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/newcastle-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">the 2-2 draw at Newcastle</a> on Saturday evening.</p><p>It left Mikel Arteta’s side six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City at the top of the Premier League but Arsenal’s manager was more concerned about Raya following an accidental collision with Newcastle’s William Osula.       <title>Champion’s corner: KC Current win first NWSL Championship with 2-1 stunner over Spirit</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/nwsl-championship-washington-spirit-kansas-city-current</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Current’s opener came direct from a corner kick</p></li><li><p>Debinha, Trinity Rodman trade goals in stoppage time</p></li><li><p>Washington Spirit lose third consecutive NWSL final</p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/21/washington-spirit-kansas-city-current-nwsl-championship-live-updates">Read Jeff Rueter’s minute-by-minute report</a></p></li></ul><p>It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.</p><p>Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute <em>Olimpico</em> from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/nwsl-championship-washington-spirit-kansas-city-current">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/manchester-city-fulham-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Manchester City are living in Premier League purgatory, without a win in four, but at least against Fulham they ended a three-game losing run. As they await their fate after being found guilty of financial breaches, their form has slumped. This passive draw was met with boos from the home fans.</p><p>Arguments will be made over Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal but City did not deserve anything more. The Norwegian uncharacteristically missed a number of fine chances as Rodrigo Muniz took advantage of City’s porous defence. They had to rely on Elliot Anderson to get anything out of the fixture.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/manchester-city-fulham-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.</p><p>It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>
